correctness.rationale: The domain is fixed and fully specified: seven nonzero vectors, seven three-point lines and fourteen ordered elements. An ideal is exactly a pair (S,T) with T contained in the full lines C(S), and rowmotion has the derived transition (P\S union support(C(S)\T), C(S)\T). An elementary count by point-set size proves 458 ideals. The seven explicit cycles in orbit_types.csv, each acted upon by all 168 invertible binary linear transformations, give pairwise disjoint families of sizes 3,42,42,35,35,105,196 covering every ideal. Thus 29 three-cycles, 35 five-cycles, and 28 seven-cycles, exact rowmotion order 105, and seven projective cycle classes. Python checks bijectivity, disjoint cover and equivariance on all 458 states x 168 maps; separately written C++ enumerates all 16384 vertex-bit masks and computes transitions from minimal absent elements, confirming the cycle counts. Both implementations executed successfully. No statement about infinite families or independent validation is made.

value.rationale: The point-below-line poset of the smallest projective plane is a natural, symmetric finite geometry rather than an arbitrary slice. Exact rowmotion orbit decomposition is a canonical invariant in dynamical algebraic combinatorics. Seven projective symmetry classes with explicit short witnesses and the unexpected coexistence of prime cycle lengths 3,5,7 (permutation order 105) provide structural information beyond counting ideals or defining rowmotion. The classification exhibits explicit non-homomesic cardinality behavior and a boundary to not-relatively-prime periodicity known for special minuscule families, while not asserting a general theorem beyond the finite object. The 458-state classification is complete and human-checkable through seven representative cycles and finite projective symmetry, not just a bare computer-generated number.
